documents.title: Coverage change
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife called: his disability approval came through and federal coverage is now primary as of January, the employer Blue Cross plan secondary. Updated registration, scanned new cards from the portal upload.

events.reason: ALS follow-up: weakness in arms and legs

reports.text: Spirometry with slow vital capacity, maximal respiratory pressures and diffusing capacity. Good effort, reproducible. FVC 74% predicted. FEV1 75% predicted. FEV1/FVC 0.80. Slow vital capacity reduced. Maximal inspiratory pressure -52 cmH2O (reduced). Maximal expiratory pressure 68 cmH2O (reduced). DLCO 88% predicted.
reports.conclusion: Reduced vital capacity with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio and reduced maximal respiratory pressures, with normal diffusing capacity: pattern of respiratory muscle weakness.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up (received)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, ALS clinic
Visit 02/07/2025

Interval: Over the past six months, more trouble with buttons and with stairs; uses the railing every time. No swallowing or speech complaints. Tolerating riluzole; PCP liver tests normal. On medical leave since October.

Exam: atrophy of the hand muscles, fasciculations in the arms, hyperreflexia in the legs. Sensory examination normal.

Pulmonary function today: FVC 74% predicted, FEV1 75%, FEV1/FVC 0.80; vital capacity reduced; MIP -52 and MEP 68 cmH2O, both reduced; DLCO normal at 88%. Restrictive pattern from respiratory muscle weakness, no intrinsic lung disease.

Plan: continue riluzole 50 mg BID. Clinic PT for home exercise and fall prevention, OT for button hook and adaptive utensils. Repeat breathing tests each visit. Return 6 months.

Meds: riluzole, lisinopril, amlodipine, octreotide LAR. NKDA.
Outside neurologist

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial preventive exam, new federal coverage through disability. Wife present.

Functional: dresses with some help for buttons, uses a button hook from OT. Bathes himself with a grab bar. Climbs stairs with the rail, slowly. No falls since we last met. Driving short distances only, wife does highway driving. Hearing and vision fine.
Cognition: intact on conversation and clock draw.
Mood: PHQ-9 4. Says the leave helped.
Home safety: rails in, bath mat, night lights. Advance directive and proxy on file from August, reviewed, unchanged.

Meds: lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, riluzole 50 BID, octreotide LAR 30 q4wk.

Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, speaks full sentences. Abdomen soft, RLQ hernia reducible. Hand intrinsic wasting, forearm fasciculations. Gait cautious, broad-based. No edema.

Plan:
- HTN/LVH: fine.
- CKD 3b: creatinine drifting up slowly over the past year; CMP and urine albumin today, follow.
- ALS: neurology/ALS clinic; PT home program.
- Carcinoid: oncology, CT due June.
- Prevention: vaccines current through fall. Colon due 2029.
- Written screening schedule given.

documents.title: Riluzole PA
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy says new drug plan needs prior auth for riluzole. Neurology is the prescriber; called their office, they will submit. Patient has 9 days of tablets left. Told wife to call us if not resolved by Friday.

events.reason: Surveillance, metastatic neuroendocrine tumor (ordered by oncology)

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Comparison 06/04/2024. Post-surgical changes of ileal resection and right hemicolectomy. The three hypervascular hepatic lesions are unchanged, largest 1.8 cm in the right lobe. No new liver lesions. No adenopathy, ascites or peritoneal disease. Small right lower quadrant fat-containing abdominal wall hernia, unchanged. Kidneys without hydronephrosis. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Stable hepatic metastases. No new disease.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP/CKD check. Oncology CT last week stable per the report (no letter yet). Says he is "holding his own." Walking with a cane outside the house now on PT's advice. Hands weaker. Talking and eating fine as far as he's concerned; wife thinks he coughs a little with water sometimes.

BP as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

HTN fine on same meds. CKD 3b: BMP today. Suggested he mention the water cough to the ALS clinic next month.

events.reason: ALS follow-up: trouble swallowing and slurred speech

documents.title: Neurology follow-up (received late)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, ALS clinic
Visit 07/25/2025 [received after records request]

Interval: Six months of gradually harder swallowing and slurred speech; sometimes chokes on thin liquids. His wife has noticed more clumsiness and several stumbles at home. No falls with injury.

Exam: tongue wasting with fasciculations. Speech nasal and spastic. Brisk jaw jerk. Increased tone in both arms with hyperreflexia. Spastic gait with cane. No sensory loss. Cognition intact.

Labs today: CBC, electrolytes, thyroid function normal; renal function at his CKD baseline.

Speech-language pathology swallow evaluation (same day): cough with thin liquids; safe with mildly thick liquids and chin-tuck. Soft, moist diet.

Discussion: bulbar progression. We discussed a feeding tube now while breathing tests allow it; he prefers to wait and will reconsider.

Plan: continue riluzole; SLP strategies; dietitian; return 6 months.

Outside neurologist

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. We have no letter from the July ALS clinic visit; history from them.

Per wife: neurology said the ALS is now affecting swallowing and speech. Speech therapist watched him drink and eat, advised thickening thin liquids and tucking his chin. Feeding tube came up; David wants to hold off. Speech is slower and more nasal to me than in June. Coughs less with the thickener. Weight down 3 kg since spring.

Exam: weight as charted. Speech nasal, effortful, understandable. Lungs clear. BP fine.

A/P:
1. ALS with bulbar involvement. Weight loss; reinforced calorie-dense soft foods per dietitian. Respect his choice on the tube; he knows the window matters. Asked records for the clinic note.
2. HTN, CKD, carcinoid: stable.
Follow up 3 months, video ok.

documents.title: Nurse visit: fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and COVID. Came in a transport chair from the lot, wife pushing; walks short distances with cane. Both shots right arm per his request. No issues after 15 minutes.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, both at their kitchen table. Consent given.

July ALS note finally came last month; matches what they told me.

Swallowing about the same with thickener. Speech harder on the screen but we managed; wife fills gaps. Using a walker inside now. Home BP 128-136/80s. Oncology visit in October fine per them, shots continuing. No new complaints. PHQ-2 1; he says the days are "slower, not darker."

Plan: same meds. In-person labs in the new year after his January ALS visit. They will call with anything.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Lisinopril 10 and amlodipine 5 refill request from pharmacy. BMP 7/2025 at neurology reported normal for him. Approved 90 days x3. Wife asked if pharmacy can deliver; gave them the pharmacy's delivery line.

results.test: Carbon dioxide [Partial pressure] in Arterial blood

reports.text: Seated spirometry. Effort limited by weakness but reproducible. FVC 60% predicted. FEV1/FVC ratio preserved. Arterial blood gas on room air drawn in the pulmonary function laboratory: pH 7.42, PaCO2 45 mmHg, PaO2 70 mmHg, HCO3 24 mmol/L.
reports.conclusion: FVC 60% predicted, declined from 74% in 02/2025; restrictive pattern of neuromuscular weakness. PaCO2 45 on room air.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up (received)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, ALS clinic
Visit 01/26/2026

Interval: Six months of steadily harder stair climbing and weaker grip; occasional slurring. His wife describes shallow breathing, worse at night, and episodes of laughing or crying he cannot stop.

Exam: sensation normal. Hand muscle atrophy, fasciculations in both arms, reflexes brisk, both plantar responses extensor.

Respiratory: ABG on room air in the PFT lab pH 7.42, PaCO2 45, PaO2 70, HCO3 24. FVC 60% predicted.

Assessment: ALS with progressive limb and bulbar weakness and now respiratory involvement, with symptoms of nocturnal hypoventilation.

Plan: Nocturnal BiPAP ordered through our respiratory therapist and a home equipment vendor. Continue riluzole. Feeding tube discussed again; still deferring. Emotional episodes discussed with patient and wife; will revisit at next visit. Return 3 months.

Outside neurologist

documents.title: BiPAP vendor
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Home equipment company called for a signed PCP face-sheet and most recent office note to go with neurology's BiPAP order. Faxed last office note and the neuro letter; PCP signed the form. Vendor setting up at home Monday.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife, in wheelchair today for the distance from the car.

ALS clinic 1/26: breathing tests down (FVC 60%, CO2 45 on the gas), BiPAP ordered for nights; machine came yesterday, first night he wore it 3 hours, then pulled it off. Wife says his breathing at night seems deeper with it on. Also told me about the laughing/crying spells neurology noted; he finds them embarrassing more than distressing.

Swallowing stable on thickened liquids. Weight down to 74. Bowels fine on octreotide.

Exam: speech slow, nasal. Breathing unlabored at rest, sat normal. Lungs clear but shallow. Heart regular. No edema. Hernia reducible.

A/P:
1. ALS with respiratory involvement: BiPAP nightly, work up to full nights; RT from vendor following.
2. HTN: BP fine.
3. CKD 3b: creatinine has been creeping up; BMP today.
4. Weight loss from bulbar disease: dietitian through clinic.
5. Advance care planning: they are thinking about what they'd want if breathing worsens; will make time at next visit.

events.reason: Lab results: potassium and kidney function

orders.reason: CKD 3b with rising creatinine and hyperkalemia

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called wife and David with yesterday's BMP: potassium 5.4, creatinine 1.98 (eGFR high 30s), down from mid 40s two years ago. No palpitations. Explained mildly high potassium with the kidneys and lisinopril both playing a part. Referring to nephrology for the decline and the potassium; until then avoid salt substitutes and big servings of high-potassium foods (handout sent). They agree.

documents.title: kidney doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is David's wife typing for him. We saw the kidney doctor on Monday. She went over his labs and said to stay on the same blood pressure pills and follow a low-potassium diet, gave us a list. Back to see her in the summer with blood work. She said she'd send you a letter.

documents.title: RE: kidney doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you, very helpful. No letter here yet; we'll ask for it. The list she gave you is the right one. See you in May.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested 3/23/26 nephrology consult note from outside nephrology. Told it would be faxed this week.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + chronic care, with wife.

Function: walker indoors, wheelchair outside. Needs help with bathing and dressing; wife and a home aide 3 mornings a week. Eating soft, thickened liquids, takes longer. BiPAP all night now; wakes clearer. Speech slow; uses a typing app sometimes. Cognition intact.
Nephrology in March advised low-potassium diet (no letter received; requested twice).
PHQ-9 4.

Meds: lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, riluzole 50 BID, octreotide LAR 30 q4wk.

Exam: BP as charted. Weight stable at 74. Lungs clear, shallow. Heart regular. No edema. Marked hand wasting, arm fasciculations.

ACP (30 min): updated his wishes with wife present. Continues BiPAP; would not want a tracheostomy or long-term ventilation. Feeding tube: still undecided. Wants to stay home. Portable medical order form discussed; he wants to think and sign at the next visit.

Plan: BMP, lipids, urine albumin today. Nephrology follow-up in August. Booked September follow-up.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up (received)
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology
Follow-up 08/10/2026

62-year-old with CKD stage 3b attributed to hypertensive nephrosclerosis, seen for routine follow-up. Says he takes lisinopril and amlodipine as prescribed. Following the low-potassium diet we reviewed at his last visit. No palpitations; no weakness beyond his established ALS pattern. Uses nocturnal BiPAP.

Other history: LVH; metastatic ileal neuroendocrine tumor on octreotide; ALS on riluzole; incisional hernia.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 132/84. Exam: no edema. Heart regular, lungs clear. Neurologic findings of ALS unchanged per patient and wife; otherwise unremarkable.

Labs today: potassium 5.6 mEq/L (H), creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (H), eGFR 35, bicarbonate 24, calcium 9.2.

Assessment: CKD 3b, slowly progressive. Hyperkalemia persisting despite dietary changes.

Plan: continue low-potassium diet. Repeat BMP in two weeks; please draw at PCP and forward. We will decide on further management with that result. Return 3 months.

Outside nephrologist
